setting: A fictional chat with a new friend at a family picnic in a park.

presentation.situation: You are at a picnic with a new friend, {{name}}. {{name}} lives with {{family}}. Talk about the people close to you, and ask about {{name}}'s family.
presentation.opening: It's so nice here. I came with {{family}}. Who do you live with?

brief.you_are: You are at a picnic with a new friend.
brief.situation: You are at a picnic with a new friend, {{name}}. {{name}} lives with {{family}}. Talk about the people close to you, and ask about {{name}}'s family.
brief.task: Talk about someone in your family using words like mother or brother, use he, she or they, and ask about the other person.
brief.done_looks_like: Your friend knows about one or two people close to you, and you asked about their family too.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are at a picnic with a new friend.
goals: Talk about someone in your family using words like mother or brother, use he, she or they, and ask about the other person.

card.want: To learn about you and to talk about their family.
card.hidden_need: Misses a brother who lives far away.
card.speech: Very simple everyday English. Short sentences. One easy question at a time.
tactics: If the answer is very short, ask one easy question
Use the person's own words back to them

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: The two of you are at a picnic in the park.
{{name}} has a brother who lives in {{city}}.

objectives.evidence: The learner names at least one family member or close person.

objectives.description: Use he, she, and they correctly
objectives.evidence: The learner uses he, she or they correctly about someone.
The learner asks a question about the friend or their family.

beats.goal: Hear who the learner lives with.
opportunity: Do you have brothers or sisters?
beats.orient: We are talking about family. Tell me one person in your family. You can say: I live with my mother.
fallback: Do you have brothers or sisters?

opportunity: Tell me about one of them. What do they do?
What is your sister or brother like?
beats.orient: Now tell me about that person. Start with he or she. For example: She works in a school.
fallback: What is your sister or brother like?
Tell me about one of them. What do they do?

opportunity: I talk too much! Is there anything you want to know about my family?
Do you want to ask me something?
beats.orient: Now ask me about my family. You can say: Do you have a brother?
fallback: Do you want to ask me something?
I talk too much! Is there anything you want to know about my family?

closing_line: Thank you. I enjoyed talking with you.

o1.good: Naming real people in your life.
o1.micro_lesson: Use family words: mother, father, brother, sister.
o1.model: I live with my parents and my sister.

o2.good: Using he for a man, she for a woman, and they for a group.
o2.micro_lesson: Choose he or she, then say one thing about the person.
o2.model: She is a teacher. She works near our house.
o2.smaller_step: Say one sentence starting with he or she.

o3.good: Asking back shows you care about the other person.
o3.micro_lesson: Use: Do you have, or: Who do you.
o3.model: Who do you live with? Do you have a brother?
o3.smaller_step: Say: Do you have a brother?

variants.name: Sana
variants.family: my mother and my two sisters
